preamble: Backing of the front rounded vowel [y] to [u] keeps rounding while retracting the tongue. In Middle English of the southern West Midlands and the Southwest, Old English /y/ often became /u/, and these u-forms entered Standard English (shut, much, cudgel), where the vowel later developed to /ʌ/. In Standard Uzbek, which lost Turkic vowel harmony under Persian influence, inherited *ü merged with /u/, so Uzbek uch, kun and yuz correspond to Turkish üç, gün and yüz.

examples.note: Old English /y/ > Middle English /u/; modern /ʌ/ by the later FOOT–STRUT split.
The variant miċel shows the competing unrounding y > i.

examples.from: Chagatai اوچ üč 'three' (< Proto-Turkic *üč; cf. Turkish üç)
examples.note: Standard Uzbek has six vowels with no front rounded series; Kipchak and Oghuz Uzbek dialects keep vowel harmony.

examples.from: Chagatai کون kün 'sun, day' (< Proto-Turkic *kün; cf. Turkish gün)
Chagatai یوز yüz 'hundred' (< Proto-Turkic *yǖŕ; cf. Turkish yüz)
